items.claim: When the script is sourced before `compinit` has run, `compdef` is undefined, so the `(( ! $+functions[compdef] ))` branch calls `_rg "$@"` at top level instead of registering the completion.
items.consequence: A user puts `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` in .zshrc above `compinit` (or above sourcing oh-my-zsh, which runs compinit). `_rg` then runs outside the completion system: every shell startup prints an error such as `_rg:NNN: command not found: _arguments`, `compdef _rg rg` is never called, and rg has no completion. This is the failure class issue #2956 was meant to remove.

items.claim: The snippet the FAQ says to add to `$HOME/.zshrc` carries a leading `$ ` prompt marker, unlike the `fpath=` snippet just above it.
items.consequence: A user copies the block verbatim into .zshrc as instructed. zsh tries to execute `$` as a command, prints `command not found: $` on every startup, and never loads the completions.

items.claim: The FAQ does not say the `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` line must come after `compinit`, although the script only registers itself when `compdef` already exists.
items.consequence: A user follows the FAQ and puts the line near the top of .zshrc, before `autoload -U compinit && compinit`, or has no compinit at all. The script takes the non-compdef branch, prints an error at startup, and `rg <TAB>` falls back to plain file completion.

items.claim: The recommended `fpath=($HOME/.zsh-complete $fpath)` instruction omits that it must precede `compinit` and that `compinit` must be run at all.
items.consequence: A user appends the `fpath=` line to the end of .zshrc, after compinit or after sourcing a framework. compinit has already scanned fpath, so `_rg` is never registered and the recommended approach silently does nothing.

items.claim: Autoload detection is hard-coded to the function name `_rg`, so the script misbehaves when installed in fpath under any other file name.
items.consequence: A user saves the output as `~/.zfunc/_ripgrep`; the `#compdef rg` tag still registers it. On the first `rg <TAB>`, `$funcstack[1]` is `_ripgrep` and compdef exists, so the script runs `compdef _rg rg` and returns no matches. Before this change `_rg "$@"` ran unconditionally and the first completion worked. Checking `$zsh_eval_context` for `loadautofunc` would not depend on the file name.

items.claim: The new condition ignores the `_RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS` test hook, so `ci/test-complete` now depends on `compdef` being undefined in the shell that sources the file.
items.consequence: `ci/test-complete` runs on a machine whose `~/.zshenv` or `/etc/zshenv` runs compinit. `( _RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS=1 source rg.zsh )` takes the `compdef _rg rg` branch, prints no arg specs, and the script fails with `Failed to get comp_args`. Adding `|| [[ -n $_RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS ]]` to the condition would make the test path explicit.

items.claim: The comment "Don't run the completion function when being sourced by itself" does not match the code, which still runs `_rg` when sourced if `compdef` is undefined.
items.consequence: A maintainer trusts the comment and assumes sourcing never invokes `_rg`. The undocumented `! $+functions[compdef]` fallback exists only for `ci/test-complete`, so someone may remove it and break CI, or keep it without realising it re-triggers the #2956 error for users who source before compinit.

items.claim: The added sentence is ungrammatical: "while this approach is easier to setup, is generally slower" is missing its subject, and "setup" should be the verb "set up".
items.consequence: User-facing documentation reads incorrectly; it should say "while this approach is easier to set up, it is generally slower than the previous method".

items.claim: The man page's SHELL COMPLETION section and the CHANGELOG "TBD" section were not updated for the new sourcing method.
items.consequence: Someone reading `man rg` still sees only "move _rg to one of your $fpath directories", and the unreleased changelog has no entry for feature #2956. The two shipped documents diverge and the feature is undiscoverable outside the FAQ.
